description:
THE INCREMENTAL BLOCKER. This is the shape that stops compiler2 from staying resident and recompiling on file change: one edit anywhere re-settles the demand of everything.

MEASURED with the new fz.compiler2.demand.cone.settled counter (added alongside this ticket), over a ladder of n identical Enum.find call sites -- complexity grows strictly linearly, so anything that does not is structural:

  n     cones  members  external  rounds  derivations  derivs/member
  1     4      14       0         14      62           4.4
  2     4      21       0         14      99           4.7
  4     4      35       0         14      167          4.8
  8     4      63       0         14      303          4.8
  16    4      119      0         14      575          4.8
  32    4      231      0         14      1119         4.8

WHAT IS ALREADY RIGHT -- do not 'fix' these:
- rounds is CONSTANT at 14. The ascent height is a property of the lattice, not the program.
- derivations per member is CONSTANT at ~4.8. The dirty-set skipping works: a member whose reads did not move is skipped.
- cones is CONSTANT at 4.
Pinned by the_demand_ascent_height_does_not_grow_with_the_program (compiler2::product_drive_test).

WHAT IS WRONG:
- members grows linearly with the program and reaches 231 of the program's 233 executables. The largest cone IS the whole program.
- external_members is 0 AT EVERY SIZE. No cone ever stands on a previously settled one. Every settle starts cold.

MECHANISM. collect_demand_cone (jobs/runtime_demand.rs:499) walks transitively from the anchor over call edges and stops only at an executable whose RuntimeDemand has ALREADY settled. Driven from a cold root, nothing has settled, so the walk does not stop until it has the entire reachable call graph. produce_runtime_demand_product then settles all of them in one atomic publication. The product key says RuntimeDemand(E) -- one executable -- and the unit of work is the program.

COST TODAY (secondary; the structure is the point). Per-settle cost grows 2.1ms -> 116.7ms across the 32x ladder, ~14% of total wall clock on the enum ladder and ~350ms of 3.1s at n=32. Derivations grow 18x over that range while time grows 54x, so per-derivation cost grows ~3x on top -- unexplained, worth its own look once the scope is fixed. Note the ascent already does O(members) work per round unconditionally (the join loop and the contributions inversion run over all members even when one member is dirty), so 14 rounds x whole program is a floor no matter how good the dirty set is.

DIRECTION -- NOT A CONE-SIZE HEURISTIC. Do not cap or chunk the cone. The question is why a cone must be collected cold at all: external_members = 0 says the reuse channel exists (collect_demand_cone stops at settled demand, and DemandGraph.external is threaded through) but never fires within a session. Establish why first. Related standing debt: fz-976 (SCC dissolution via a settled-group epoch fact) and the note that the SCC-settled demand solver is a removal target, not a precedent to extend.

CHECKS: external_members > 0 on the ladder; members for a cone anchored at a leaf executable is small; the flat numbers above stay flat; lib + matrix at baseline.
title: RuntimeDemand is keyed per executable but computed per program: the demand cone spans the whole reachable call graph and never reuses a settled one
